recognize_zh: 低倍視野中許多紅血球內有細小的環狀及梨形寄生蟲，部分紅血球含兩個以上蟲體，紅血球間散佈小型蟲體，紅血球大小正常且無瘧色素或配子體，符合巴貝西蟲（Babesia）感染。
features: Many red cells with small intraerythrocytic ring, dot and pyriform organisms
Several red cells containing two or more parasites
Small extracellular purple forms scattered between red cells (some likely platelets)
Infected red cells normal in size; no hemozoin pigment, schizonts or gametocytes
Tetrad forms not resolvable at this magnification
Occasional crenated red cells (echinocytes), likely artifactual
describe_en: Giemsa-stained peripheral blood smear viewed at low magnification shows numerous red cells containing small ring, dot and pyriform intraerythrocytic organisms, with several red cells containing two or more parasites. Small extracellular purple forms are present between red cells, some of which are likely platelets. Infected red cells are not enlarged, and there is no hemozoin pigment, schizont or gametocyte formation; tetrads cannot be resolved at this power. Scattered crenated red cells are likely artifactual, and no leukocytes are present in this field. Findings are consistent with Babesia infection; high-power review for tetrads and PCR confirmation are recommended.

ddx.vs: P. falciparum rings are often double-chromatin or appliqué forms accompanied by banana-shaped gametocytes or pigment, without extracellular organisms or tetrads.
Superimposed platelets are granular with a surrounding clear halo and lie out of the red cell plane, rather than forming delicate rings within the cell.
Pappenheimer bodies are small clustered basophilic granules at the red cell periphery that are iron positive, not ring-shaped organisms.
